svg.text: HOW TO MAKE IT AND HOW IT FITS

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Make two, both the same. Solder the sensor carrier to a 3-core sealed

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: outdoor lead (1-Wire: data, ground and supply), 2 m for the steel

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: probe and 3 m for the air probe.

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Push the carrier to the closed end of the sheath, sensor face down,

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: with a dab of thermal paste between the sensor and the sheath end.

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Fill the sheath with potting epoxy from the closed end up, with no

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: air pockets; fit heat-shrink with adhesive over the sheath mouth.

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Steel probe: lies on the bottom flange top, 6.5 from the tip, held by

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: a spring-steel flange clip with thermal paste under it.

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Air probe: hangs on its lead between the girders, in shade.

text.font-family: IBM Plex Sans, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Check each probe in ice water: 0 degC within 0.5 degC (R5).
